annotationRationale: The derivation uses the distance-speed-time relationship and subtracts the first two distances from the total. Converting minutes to hours keeps the units consistent.
sourceMethod: Follows the official method of calculating the first two distances, finding the remaining distance, and dividing by half an hour.

review.mathCheck: Each interval lasts 1/2 hour. The first two distances are 30 and 32.5 miles, leaving 33.5 miles. Dividing by 1/2 hour gives 67 mph, choice D. This uses interval averages and requires no constant-speed assumption.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, mathematically faithful adaptation of official solution #2 on page 2, preserving the distance calculations, remaining-distance subtraction, and final average-speed division.
review.annotationCheck: The quantitative relationship is assessed, while time conversion is supporting knowledge. Units and all three intervals are handled explicitly.
